haiku-low.q1: When the caller's transaction commits, a pending row is inserted into the monolith notifications table. The row exists only if that transaction commits.
haiku-low.q2: It redelivers the message, possibly to a different consumer, if it is not acknowledged within 30 seconds.
haiku-low.q3: Five attempts. Waits of 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes before attempts 2 to 5. Then the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q4: One at a time, behind a flag: shipping_update, then order_confirmed, then password_reset. Before password_reset, order_confirmed must run on the service 3+ days with measured p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay under 60 seconds.
haiku-low.q5: The notification id, passed as idempotency_key. It comes from the row's id. MailRelay drops a repeat accepted within 24 hours and still returns success.
haiku-low.q6: A monolith forwarder publishes pending rows to the broker. The service stores, renders, sends and publishes a result. The monolith marks the row forwarded after broker confirmation; the result consumer later copies the outcome.
haiku-low.q7: The flag notif.route.<type>, read by the monolith. The old worker checks it at the start of each batch; the forwarder re-checks it after taking the row lock.
haiku-low.q8: The service's notifications table, keyed by notification id, with INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a known id is never re-sent. MailRelay's idempotency key also drops repeats within 24 hours.
haiku-low.q9: After storing the message in a service-DB transaction, it acks. A crash before commit means no ack and redelivery. A crash after commit but before ack means redelivery, a no-op conflict, then ack.
haiku-low.q10: In the service notifications table, as attempts and next_attempt_at. The service's sender loop acts on it, sending a row only when next_attempt_at is due.
haiku-low.q11: Forwarded rows stay with the service and are still completed by it; the old worker never picks them up. Unforwarded pending rows go back to the old worker.
haiku-low.q12: id, type, user_id, email, payload, created_at, attempts, next_attempt_at. The email content is rendered in the service from copied templates, not in the monolith.

sonnet.q1: When the caller's transaction commits: enqueue_notification inserts a pending row into the monolith notifications table inside that transaction. The row exists only if the caller's transaction commits.
sonnet.q2: It redelivers the message (if not acknowledged within 30 s), possibly to a different consumer (at-least-once).
sonnet.q3: 5 attempts total, with waits of 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes before attempts 2 to 5. After the fifth failure the row is marked failed and on-call is paged.
sonnet.q4: One type at a time behind a flag: shipping_update first, then order_confirmed, then password_reset. Each needs at least 3 days of soak with clean checks (and a day-1 rollback drill for shipping_update) before the next. Before password_reset moves, order_confirmed must have run on the service 3 or more days with its measured p99 enqueue-to-MailRelay latency under 60 s over that time.
sonnet.q5: idempotency_key, set to the notification id (row.id). MailRelay, if it already accepted a send with the same key in the last 24 h, drops the new send and still returns success, so the caller cannot tell a duplicate from a first send.
sonnet.q6: Business code writes a pending row to the monolith notifications table; a monolith forwarder (polling every 1 s) publishes pending rows of service-routed types to the broker (notifications.requested), waits for the broker confirmation, sets status='forwarded' and commits. The monolith's part is done at that point (it never sends that row afterwards); it later only copies the result message (sent/failed, attempts) into its row. The reconciler republishes forwarded rows older than 1 hour with no result.
sonnet.q7: The monolith, via the per-type flag notif.route.<type> (monolith or service, default monolith). The old worker reads the flags at the start of each batch and the forwarder re-checks the flag after taking the row lock. The ownership transition pending to forwarded happens under the row lock (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), so a row's owner is fixed when the forwarder commits forwarded. The service never reads the flag.
sonnet.q8: The service's notifications table has the notification id as primary key and the consumer does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING, so a duplicate is a no-op (acked). Also every send passes idempotency_key = id, which MailRelay dedupes within 24 h. Service rows are kept at least 30 days.
sonnet.q9: The ack comes after the insert, in the same service-DB transaction commit; sending happens later in a separate sender loop, not at consume time. Crash before commit: no ack, broker redelivers. Crash after commit but before ack: redelivery hits the conflict, no-op, ack.
sonnet.q10: In the service notifications table (attempts and next_attempt_at columns, copied from the message at handoff). The service sender loop acts on it: it polls every 1 s, claims one due row, and sends only when next_attempt_at is due; failed attempts 1 to 4 update next_attempt_at, attempt 5 sets failed.
sonnet.q11: Rows already forwarded stay with the service: the old worker never picks them up and the service finishes them and returns results. Only unforwarded (pending) rows go back to the old worker. No row is lost or sent twice.
sonnet.q12: The notifications.requested message: id, type, user_id, email, payload, created_at, attempts, next_attempt_at. The email content is rendered in the service (templates copied into the service), not in the monolith.
